symmetryCheck: The identical lens was run on the UPA (2004–14) and on the BJP-led Union (2014–26). It produces the same pattern in both: the UPA's two largest one-off distributions (ADWDRS Feb 2008, NFSA Jul 2013) fell 13.5 and 9 months before general elections, with opposite results (won 2009, lost 2014); the NDA's PM-KISAN (Feb 2019) and the Nov 2023 cluster fell 1.5 and 5 months before general elections, again with mixed results (BJP +21 in 2019, −63 in 2024). Pre-poll timing is therefore non-discriminating between parties (2/3 UPA events vs 6/12 NDA events within 12 months of a general election) and weakly predictive of outcomes (2/3). What differs is form, not timing: the UPA's instruments were statutory or one-off (NREGA, NFSA, waiver), the NDA's are recurring PM-branded transfers with instalment events (PM-KISAN 23 releases, 'Modi ki guarantee'). The lens also produced an equally uncomfortable picture for the control I had no theory about — the NSAP pension — which no government raised across five elections. Assembly-poll proximity was not used as a base rate because with ~5–8 state elections a year almost any month is within 12 months of one; it is non-discriminating by construction.
